subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls, rate limits & routing
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.p@enterpriseco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls, rate limits & routing

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned on the goals and next steps. I’ve highlighted the pain points you shared, your current stack, and what success looks like for EnterpriseCo.

Pain points we heard
- Per-tenant cost and latency variability across high-traffic customers
- Need for fine-grained rate limits and quotas per customer and per API key
- Difficulty routing heavy customers to specific hardware or regions for compliance/perf
- Lack of visibility into token-level cost by customer and route

Current stack & constraints
- In-house proxy + internal model serving in GCP (K80/one older instance type)
- PostgreSQL for tenant metadata; no centralized policy engine today
- Security: SSO via Okta, enterprise requires SOC2 evidence and audit logs

Success criteria (what you told us)
1) Per-customer routing/pinning so top 3 customers can be routed to dedicated pools (region: us-west)
2) Enforce tiered rate limits and quotas (bronze/silver/gold) with burst allowances
3) Token-level cost reporting and billing export (daily)
4) Audit logs and transplantable evidence for procurement/SOC2 review

Proposed next steps
- Redwood to share short tech note on how dedicated pools + routing policies work (attached whitepaper).
- Schedule technical deep dive with your infra lead (Laura suggested Thu or Fri next week).
- Send over current tenant list and top traffic customer IDs for preliminary capacity planning (we’ll use MAP_v1.xlsx template).
- Provide HubSpot deal link and procurement checklist for your team to track (link below).

Attachments: redwood-multi-tenancy-whitepaper.pdf, MAP_v1.xlsx

If anything above is off, flag and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll book the deep dive once you confirm availability.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.p@enterpriseco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls, rate limits & routing

Ben — thanks for the clear summary. Couple of clarifications:
1) For routing: we need the ability to pin a customer to a specific GPU pool but also to automatically fall back to shared pools if reserved capacity is exhausted.
2) Rate limits: we'd like per-tenant burst allowances that reset per minute and hard daily quotas per tenant. Can Redwood enforce both?
3) Compliance: procurement will want an example of audit logs showing request-level metadata for a 30-day window.

We’re available for a technical session Fri 17th (US-PST) morning. I’ll loop in procurement next.

—Sanjay
Head of Platform Engineering, EnterpriseCo

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.p@enterpriseco.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls, rate limits & routing

Sanjay — great questions. Short answers: yes to both, with implementation notes below. Looping in Laura (infra/solutions) and Marissa (CS) to own the technical and onboarding bits.

Routing & fallback
- Redwood supports policy-based routing: you can pin tenants to pools and set fallback rules when capacity is low. Fallback can be to a compatible quantized model or a shared pool in another region. We’ll include a sample policy in the tech deep dive.

Rate limits & quotas
- We support per-tenant rate limits with hierarchical rules (per-minute burst + daily hard quota). Limits are enforced at the gateway and replicated to all serving nodes to avoid split-brain.

Audit logs & exports
- Audit logs include request id, tenant id, model, latency, tokens consumed, and route. We can provide a 30-day export sandbox for procurement review and a sample SOC2 evidence pack.

Next actions before Friday deep dive:
- Sanjay: attach current tenant list + top 10 by qps into MAP_v1.xlsx (you noted procurement will be looped in).
- Ben/Redwood: prepare short runbook and sample routing policy + cost example for pinned vs shared routing.
- Laura: can you prepare a quick note on expected throughput sizing for pinned pools (rough baseline calc)?

I’ll book Fri 17th, 10:00 AM PST unless you prefer a different time.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay.p@enterpriseco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 07:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls, rate limits & routing

Hi all — quick technical notes ahead of today’s deep dive:

Sizing baseline for pinned pools (very rough):
- If top customers have sustained 250 qps with 200-token avg responses, estimate ~3x batching headroom per GPU for latency SLOs. For typical LLMs that maps to ~1 A100-equivalent per ~150 qps baseline (will refine with model specifics).

Policy examples I’ll bring:
- JSON-style routing policy (tenant -> pool, fallback rules, allowed regions).
- Rate-limit hierarchy (tenant overrides > plan defaults).

Security/compliance:
- We can enable per-tenant KMS keys and stream audit logs to your SIEM. For SOC2 evidence we provide a signed export with request-level metadata.

See you at 10:00 AM PST.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
